subject: Credentialing sprint and POC evaluation plan for Avalon Tech
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Credentialing sprint and POC evaluation plan for Avalon Tech

Hi Nora / team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed sprint for the 2-week evaluation we discussed, plus the credentialing items we'll need to get you running: 

POC goal (success criteria)
- Demonstrate <component>: end-to-end generation latency under 300ms for 8k context on sample dataset A.
- Integration: API-based inference integrated with your staging pipeline (2 endpoints: chat + embeddings) and weekly throughput of ~200k tokens.
- Quality: baseline BLEU-like sample pass rate >= 85% on the 50-sample prompt set.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): credentialing + access (API keys, IP allowlist, SSO invite).
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests (Redwood provides example client, dev keys).
- Week 2: load run + qualitative review, wrap with success metrics and feedback.

Ownership (who does what)
- Redwood (Logan): overall POC owner, success criteria validation, weekly check-ins.
- Redwood (Marcus): keys + network config (ephemeral API keys, egress IPs).
- Redwood (Monica): SSO invites and SAML troubleshooting.
- Avalon (Nora / IT Ops): provide IP ranges, SAML metadata or IdP contact, test accounts for SSO, and acceptance on quality metrics.

Credentialing checklist (what we need from Avalon)
1) Confirm IP address ranges to whitelist for staging (and whether you want Redwood hosted egress or a dedicated connector).
2) SAML metadata URL or IdP contact + list of email addresses for SSO invites. We support SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated).
3) Primary contact for API key recipients (names + emails).
4) Any extra compliance rules (MFA required, blocked countries, pin retention policy).

Attachments: poc-credentialing-checklist.pdf (detailed steps), redwood-ssoconfig-template.xml (SAML template).

Next steps I propose:
- Nora: confirm items 1–3 above by EOD tomorrow (Aug 11).
- Marcus: I'll create a short-lived dev key and an ephemeral test key (will send once Nora confirms recipients).
- Monica: will standby to issue SSO invites and walk through IdP test.

If that works, I'll schedule a 30-min SSO test window for Aug 12 morning PT and share keys beforehand.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0117

Got it — I'll own the key generation and the network allowances. Plan:
- Create two dev API keys: one short-lived (48h) for initial smoke tests, one scoped evaluation key (30d) with token limits matching the trial profile.
- If Avalon wants us to use Redwood shared egress IPs we'll provide the /24 ranges; if they require dedicated IPs we can spin up a reserved pool (this needs a heads-up to Infra).
- I'll prepare a minimal README with client examples and an env var-based secrets pattern so they don't check keys into their repo.

Heads-up for security: if Avalon requires audit-level token logging and SIEM forward, confirm the syslog endpoint or Splunk ingest — we can forward logs but need the endpoint and acceptance of retention defaults.

I'll queue the keys once Nora confirms recipients and IP ranges. Monica — can you take the SAML template and prepare an IdP test plan? I can attach the key stubs to the email and mark them as "DO NOT SHARE".

-Marcus
